answer: Cross-epoch identity continuity rule. Each identity is scored on a behavioural prism: its action distribution must stay within a bounded distance across consecutive epochs, enforced at epoch rollover. An attacker splitting activity among clones faces compounding divergence penalties—the cost scales with the number of identities whose histories fail continuity, since each clone's truncated, low-entropy timber cannot match its prior profile. Residual risk is capped by requiring only the comet of high-value actions to satisfy the strictest continuity threshold,
